title: Tail scan reaches its exit state
statement: Let $y$ and $w$ be finite bit strings, let $i,k,p,q$ be natural numbers, let $e$ be a Boolean, and let $	ext{last}$ be either a bit or absent. Suppose $y$ with its first $i$ bits removed is $w$, $i\le |y|$, $k\le |y|+1$, and $q\le |\mathrm{bits}(k)|$, where $\mathrm{bits}(k)$ is the binary word for $k$. Starting from the configuration with input $y$, input head at position $1$, work tapes storing the binary words for $i,0,k,p$, and head positions $0,0,q,0$, there is a finite safe computation in the access machine (with parameter $\mathrm{mode}$) to the configuration whose state is the exit determined by recursively scanning $w$ against the binary word for $k$ with its first $q$ bits removed, updating the Boolean comparison and last-bit data according to the scan; the final work tapes store the binary words for $0,0,k,p$ and all head positions are zero.
hypotheses_covered: $e$ is Boolean and last is optional Boolean
$y$ with its first $i$ bits removed equals $w$
caveat: The private recursive scan and configuration-path predicates have no informal definitions supplied, so their transition details are summarized from the formal definitions.
